answer: Require each agent to earn trust the way a marble quarry earns its mark: by doing slow, checkable work that cannot be faked at scale. A newcomer deposits a small bond, then completes useful tasks verified by a rotating jury of unrelated peers, each verdict sealed with a distinct cipher so no jury can be copied or bought wholesale. A fable of instant reputation fails here because trust accrues only from diverse, repeated confirmations bound to one key. Sybil farms must fund a bond, redo real work, and bribe fresh juries for every clone, which costs more than honest participation pays.
